verified_picks.title: Quantitative Analyst, New Product Development - Morningstar Indexes (REQ-058340)
verified_picks.http_status: 200 (browser page) + 200 (Workday CXS API, posted 2026-09-10, no endDate)
verified_picks.reason: The only pick that survives adversarial reading intact. I pulled the full JD from the Workday API and every quote in the screen is verbatim-accurate. 'Up to 2 years of experience' is genuinely a CEILING, not a floor - the only India req in the set structured to exclude senior people. 'Bachelor's degree in a quantitative, financial discipline, or engineering' names engineering explicitly. MBA and CFA Level II are both explicitly 'preferred', not required, so neither is a knockout. Python/R/MATLAB + SQL is only 'desirable'. Where I downgrade it: 'Knowledge of institutional investing, modern portfolio theory, and portfolio construction processes' appears FLAT in Requirements with no softening word attached - I checked, the word 'desirable' attaches only to the programming bullet, not this one - and he has literally none of it beyond one Computational Finance course. That is a required line he fails today, and it is the reason this is 70 not 80. It is also the one flat gap on the whole list that 3-5 weeks of free Morningstar/MSCI methodology reading plus one built factor index genuinely closes. Timing caveat is real: immediate-start req, degree not conferred until May 2027.

verified_picks.title: Senior Quantitative Analyst - New Product Development - Morningstar Indexes (REQ-057918)
verified_picks.reason: REFUTED on the explicit seniority axis. 'Senior' is in the title. The screen's defence is that no years bullet appears in the posted requirements - I verified that is true - but a title carrying Senior is exactly the hidden-seniority case, and a candidate with zero full-time employment applying to it is binned on the first pass. The screen refutes itself: its own gaps field says 'without a referral a fresher CV gets binned regardless of the literal bullets', which is an admission that eligible is not 'stretch'. Second hit: 'Proficiency in working with large, complex tables under Postgres, SQL Server' sits in the flat Requirements list with no preferred qualifier, and he has neither Postgres nor SQL Server named anywhere - strong generic SQL and SQLAlchemy is not the same claim. keep=false is NOT 'ignore this req' - it means do not spend a separate application slot on it. It is the same team, same office and almost certainly the same hiring manager as REQ-058340, so the one referral conversation already covers it; let the referrer route him to whichever level is open.

verified_picks.title: Morningstar Development Program - Equity Research, Chicago (REQ-058267)
verified_picks.http_status: 200 (browser page) + 200 (CXS API, posted 2026-09-08). JD confirms 'This role will be posted until October 5, 2026'
verified_picks.reason: The screen's factual claims check out and its score does not. Verified verbatim in the JD: 'A bachelor's degree to be completed no later than May 2027', 'We are accepting applicants with zero to two years of full-time work experience', 'we welcome all fields of study', base $83,000, closes 5 Oct 2026. I also searched the full text and confirmed there is NO 'unrestricted right to work in the U.S.' clause - the screen is right about that. What I refute is the inference drawn from it. Calling the missing clause 'an omission he can exploit' is wishful: this is a cohort-based US campus programme, Chicago-only, at an entry-level US salary, and Workday's own application form carries the standard sponsorship knockout question. Scoring it 84 - the single highest score at the entire company - for a Mumbai candidate who needs an H-1B is the screen flattering him, and it buries the decisive disqualifier down in 'gaps' where a reader skims past it. keep=true only in a strict sense: the posted criteria genuinely do not exclude him, the graduation window is his exact month, and the deadline forces the decision inside 11 days. Cap it at 30-45 minutes. Do NOT do the 10-hour equity research writing sample the screen recommends - that is real effort spent on a ~1% outcome.

verified_picks.title: Morningstar Development Program - Rotational Track (Campus), Chicago (REQ-058222)
verified_picks.http_status: 200 (browser page) + 200 (CXS API, posted 2026-09-08). JD confirms 'This role will be posted until October 5, 2026'
verified_picks.reason: Verified: the Requirements block really is just two lines - 'A bachelor's degree' and 'A resume is required to apply' - and there is no work-authorisation clause and no graduation-year bullet. Base $71,667. So the posted bar is met. Same refutation as REQ-058267 and slightly worse: the title literally says '(Campus)', which is US campus recruiting, and with no stated graduation year the cohort is most likely built around candidates who start in 2027 from US schools. Scoring this 80 is score inflation on a req whose entire requirement list is 'have a degree'. Low posted bar is not the same as high odds. keep=true purely because it is the same resume in the same sitting, ~15 extra minutes, same 5 Oct deadline. Declare the sponsorship need honestly on the form.

verified_picks.title: Data Scientist, AI & ML Data Collection - PitchBook (REQ-058054)
verified_picks.reason: The hardest refutation on the list, and the screen's worst call - it told him to spend his one warm intro here. I pulled the JD and the decisive structural fact is that the 'Skills and Qualifications' block is ONE FLAT LIST with no preferred section. Only two lines carry a softener: 'Familiarity with cloud ML environments... is beneficial' and 'experience with financial data... is a plus'. Everything else is required. He fails THREE required lines, not the one soft years gap the screen describes. (1) '2+ years of experience in applied data science, machine learning, NLP, or information extraction' - he has ~13 months of internships. (2) 'Demonstrated experience taking a data science or machine learning solution from problem definition and experimentation through production launch and ongoing improvement' - he has zero production ownership; LawzyAI having a live URL is not launch, monitoring, regression investigation and drift. (3) 'Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience using pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and PyTorch or TensorFlow' - the conjunction is 'and', making PyTorch/TensorFlow required, and he has neither. A referral waives a years number. It does not waive a years number AND a production-ownership requirement AND a framework he has never opened. Do not spend the referral here.

verified_picks.title: Operations Associate - International Wealth Platform (REQ-057577)
verified_picks.reason: Survives, with one omission corrected. The Eligibility block the screen quotes is real and verbatim: 'Graduation and above in any discipline' and 'Candidates with up to 2 years of experience can apply'. 'Any discipline' genuinely removes the finance-degree filter. But the screen quoted only that block and not the separate Requirements block below it, which narrows the same number to 'Up to 2 years of experience IN THE FINANCIAL SERVICES INDUSTRY' and lists 'An understanding of the Financial Services marketplace that applies to Wealth Managers' as a flat requirement, not an advantage. He has roughly 4 months of fintech-adjacent exposure (CypherSOL, Bigul), so he is inside the ceiling but not clean against the domain line. Not a refutation - the number is still a ceiling and the discipline door is still open, which makes this one of only two India reqs whose posted bar he can actually clear. Honest caveats the screen states correctly: degree must be conferred, so this is a March-April 2027 application, the shift is 12pm-9pm, and the work is ticket-queue operations rather than the analytics he wants.

verified_picks.title: Compliance Analyst, Conflicts of Interest, Global Controls (REQ-058381)
verified_picks.http_status: 200 (browser page) + 200 (CXS API, posted 2026-09-16, legal entity DBRS Ratings GmbH Branch India)
verified_picks.reason: Verified and it holds - this is the lowest posted bar of any analyst-titled role at Morningstar India. Confirmed verbatim: 'At least 1 years' experience in operations, roles associated with standardization or experience in an operational business environment' (his ~13 months honestly clears it), 'Bachelor's degree is required' (no discipline named), and critically 'Background or experience in process automation or AI implementation is preferred' - confirmed as preferred, and it is his single strongest line anywhere at this company, one almost no compliance applicant can match. The control-room bullet is correctly flagged 'would be an advantage', which is exactly why the Analyst version beats the Associate twin. Two flat lines he fails that the screen soft-pedalled: 'Knowledge of securities and the finance industry' and 'Experience in working with corporate policies, procedures and other guidance documents' both appear with no preferred/advantage qualifier. NISM Series-III A at ~Rs 1,500 closes the first honestly. The screen's own career caveat is the right one and I endorse it: this is compliance operations, a bridge into the building, not the BI/analytics job he wants. Note I did not verify the twin req AP-24869531 - confirm it exists before counting on the double-application trick.

verified_picks.title: Product Consultant, Client Service (REQ-058048)
verified_picks.reason: REFUTED on the experience floor, which is the first thing a recruiter screens. Requirements opens with '2-3 years of relevant experience' - a floor, not a ceiling - against his ~13 months of internships and no client-service or capital-markets desk time at all. By the standard applied here that is a 'no', not a 'stretch'. Credit where due: I grepped the JD and the screen's Skills block quote is completely accurate - 'API Testing (via Postman), Using Inspect in web pages to identify data mappings/source, Reading JSON/XML, Splunk, FTP Delivery mechanisms, IP whitelisting' is verbatim, and he genuinely could cross all of it in under a week. But that block sits above a hard years floor, and the fund-structure lines in the same block (SICAVs, Life and Pension wrappers, option chain, duration, risk statistics) are blank for him. Also weigh the condition the screen correctly surfaced: 'Availability to work on Saturdays, Sundays & Public holidays (on a rotating basis) is a key requirement' in a 24x7 support operation. Not worth an application slot.

verified_picks.title: Specialist, Level II (Data Level II) (REQ-057638)
verified_picks.reason: REFUTED twice over. The very first Requirements line is 'Bachelor's degree or above in finance/business with knowledge in fund investment data' - a flat degree-DISCIPLINE requirement naming finance or business, and he is B.Tech CSE with zero fund investment data knowledge. That is not a soft preference he can argue around; it is the opening filter. Second, 'A minimum of 1-3 years of experience working in similar profiles' is a floor he is under. Third, the title carries 'Level II'. The screen scored this 56 and called it 'stretch' on the strength of soft-skill bullets about analysis and communication, which is precisely the kind of why_fit that collapses in a 30-second screen when the reader's eye lands on the degree line. Add a US shift. Skip it.

verified_picks.title: Analyst, Morningstar Credit Analytics - CMBS (REQ-058210)
verified_picks.reason: Screen's 'no' confirmed from the live JD, and I would go lower still. The Requirements block is only five lines, and the first is '1-3 years' relevant experience in the credit research domain, with working knowledge of CMBS transactions' - the domain is ANDed to the years, so both must be true and both are zero for him. 'Master's degree, CFA, or FRM preferred' adds a credential wall on top. The screen's argument for listing it is that the tooling bar is uniquely low ('Intermediate-level Excel skills' is the only tool named, which I confirmed) - true, but a low tooling bar is irrelevant when the domain requirement is a specialist one that cannot be faked in front of a ratings analyst. Skip entirely unless someone inside Morningstar Credit Analytics explicitly invites him.

honesty_check: Mostly honest on facts, dishonest in its ranking. Every verbatim quote I spot-checked against the live Workday API was real, including the ones easiest to fabricate: the Splunk/Postman/IP-whitelisting skills block on REQ-058048, the 'bachelor's degree to be completed no later than May 2027' line, the 'Up to 2 years' ceiling on REQ-058340, and the Apprentice REQ-057801 exclusion (confirmed verbatim: 'Only candidates graduating in 2026... BE/B. Tech, Postgraduate, and Master's degree holders are not eligible to apply'). That sourcing is better than most screens. Where it overreached, in order of harm. (1) It gave the two Chicago MDP reqs 84 and 80 - the highest and joint-second scores at the entire company - to a Mumbai candidate who cannot legally work in Chicago, then filed the disqualifier under 'gaps'. Calling the absent work-auth clause 'an omission he can exploit' is flattery dressed as legal analysis. (2) It called PitchBook REQ-058054 'the best technical fit in the company' and told him to spend his one warm intro there, having read a flat qualification list as though it had a preferred section - he fails three required lines there (2+ years, production launch ownership, PyTorch/TensorFlow), not one soft years gap. That recommendation would have burned his single most valuable asset. (3) Eight of eleven picks are graded 'stretch', which is a hedge rather than a screen; five of those eight are hard no's on posted floors or title seniority. (4) REQ-057918 is graded 'stretch' while its own gaps field concedes a fresher CV 'gets binned regardless of the literal bullets'. (5) On REQ-057577 it quoted the friendly Eligibility block and omitted the Requirements block directly beneath it that narrows the same number to financial services experience. (6) One dead link out of eleven (REQ-058334), hidden because Workday returns HTTP 200 for pulled reqs - I only caught it via the CXS API. Its strategic core, though, is correct and I did not find a way to break it: there is genuinely no India campus channel, no posted Jan-May internship, and the Apprentice door is explicitly barred to him, so referral-first into Indexes NPD is the right conclusion.
final_recommendation: This week, spend 45 minutes total filing both Chicago MDP applications (REQ-058267 then REQ-058222, same resume, one sitting) before the verified 5 October 2026 deadline, declaring sponsorship honestly - treat them as capped lottery tickets and skip the 10-hour equity research writing sample the screen wanted. Then stop applying to Morningstar entirely until 2027, because every India req is an immediate-start experienced-hire posting and a September 2026 application saying 'available June 2027' dies on availability before anyone reads a line. Through October-December, do two things only: open one referral conversation inside Morningstar Indexes New Product Development in Navi Mumbai - that single contact covers REQ-058340 and REQ-057918 and any re-post - and spend 3-5 weeks closing the one flat requirement standing between him and REQ-058340 by reading Morningstar's own free index methodology PDFs and building one rules-based factor index on NSE data, written up as a four-page methodology document. Submit to REQ-058340 or its successor in December 2026-February 2027 with that document attached; the req has re-posted continuously through 2026, so a live version will exist. Hold REQ-058381 (Compliance Analyst, lowest posted bar at the company, and his automation/AI experience is a genuine differentiator there) and REQ-057577 as February-April 2027 fallbacks, and do not spend an application slot on the other five.
